document_title: Fairbanks So Far. A 123-Vote Lead, 1,235 Ballots Out
post_copy:
The unofficial Fairbanks results printed at 9:57 a.m. on October 7th carry two columns of zeros, absentee and questioned.

How does Alexis Howell lead Miguel Ramirez by 123 in Seat D? Ramirez won Election Day by 639. Howell won early voting by 762. Seat H's lead came the same way.

Can the zeros change Seat D? They could. Up to 1,235 ballots are due to fill those columns at 2 p.m. on October 13th.

Is it a data center vote? Not directly, and a lead isn't a mandate. The Assembly asked the state for an AI data center moratorium. Howell agreed with one. Seat H leader Scott Crass voted for it. Ramirez wanted more study.

Election Day is set against early voting, then 32 precincts, the Eielson precinct's 24 ballots and every unofficial total.

If the leads hold, what can the winners fairly say voters told them about data centers?

#FairbanksBorough #DataCenterMoratorium #AbsenteeBallots

A note on the numbers. Every result here is unofficial. The 639 and 762 margins are arithmetic on the clerk's rows (6,251 minus 5,612, and 1,618 minus 856), and so is the count of 27 precincts that went the same way in all three seats. The 9:57 a.m. stamp is the summary report's print time.
Voted in Fairbanks, worked the count or sat in on the Assembly? Add what the records leave out below.
Every Alaska AI decision on the public docket, with its live dates, is at https://alaskaaihq.com

slides.body: In 11, Election Day chose Howell, LaJiness and Crass. In 16, it chose Ramirez, Shupe and Leaders.

aftercare: Post before the count. The draft arrives Saturday, October 10th, and the deck goes stale at 2 p.m. on Tuesday, October 13th. Post Monday, October 12th, 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time, which gives the deck a full day before the count. Don't post it after the count without updating it.
Paste the first comment (sources, the note on the numbers, the context invite and the site line) within 60 seconds of posting.

Reply to every comment in the first hour. Never call the result final or say who won. Every number is unofficial until the October 22nd certification, and the 1,235 outstanding ballots can't be assumed to favour either candidate.

Watch the October 13th 2 p.m. count at https://www.fnsb.gov/elections. If Seat D flips, edit the post or delete it the same day. If it holds, add a dated comment with the new totals instead of rewriting the caption.

If a reader calls it a data center referendum, point out that the post says a lead isn't a mandate. If someone says the moratorium covers Eielson, the resolution text names only state-owned or municipal land (slide 06).
After 48 hours, note the saves, comments and reposts so the ledger can learn from them.
editor_notes_for_email: The caption is the room's winner with the critic's one fix, shipped byte for byte with its hashtag line. It says the Assembly asked for an "AI data center moratorium", which is KUAC's label (C53); Resolution 2026-25 itself says new commercial data centers on state-owned or municipal lands and never says AI, and the first comment says so. Margins 639 and 762 and the 27 of 32 precinct count are showrunner arithmetic on the clerk's primary rows (C74, C75, C80). Every result is unofficial and the deck never claims a mandate.
